**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-3595177, Reactome:R-HSA-2022870)

**Proposed mechanism:** CHSY1 (HGNC:2353) —DISRUPTS→ Extracellular matrix proteoglycan biosynthesis; BGN (HGNC:1065) —DISRUPTS→ Extracellular matrix proteoglycan biosynthesis; Extracellular matrix proteoglycan biosynthesis —LEADS_TO→ Skeletal abnormalities (HP:0000001); Extracellular matrix proteoglycan biosynthesis —LEADS_TO→ Abnormal limbs (HP:0000001). Loss-of-function mutations in CHSY1 and BGN disrupt the shared pathway of extracellular matrix proteoglycan biosynthesis, leading to skeletal abnormalities and abnormal limb development characteristic of both temtamy preaxial brachydactyly syndrome and Meester-Loeys syndrome.

**How to falsify it:** Demonstration that mutations in CHSY1 and BGN in these conditions lead to functionally opposite effects (e.g., one requires gain-of-function while the other requires loss-of-function) or that the affected molecular pathways are entirely distinct and non-overlapping. _(variant: Identification of pathogenic variants in CHSY1 or BGN with a population frequency > 0.1% in gnomAD.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared molecular underpinnings of temtamy preaxial brachydactyly syndrome and Meester-Loeys syndrome, particularly their convergence on extracellular matrix proteoglycan biosynthesis, could pave the way for targeted therapeutic strategies aimed at ameliorating skeletal and limb defects. Therapies that modulate proteoglycan synthesis or function could potentially benefit patients with either condition.

#### 6. Wagner disease  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.433)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-3595177, Reactome:R-HSA-2022870)

**Proposed mechanism:** CHSY1 (HGNC:2408) —DISRUPTS→ proteoglycan biosynthesis (GO:0000223); VCAN (HGNC:12721) —DISRUPTS→ proteoglycan biosynthesis (GO:0000223); proteoglycan biosynthesis (GO:0000223) —LEADS_TO→ extracellular matrix organization (GO:0030198); extracellular matrix organization (GO:0030198) —LEADS_TO→ Skeletal dysplasia (HP:0005111); extracellular matrix organization (GO:0030198) —LEADS_TO→ Retinal abnormalities (HP:0000501). Loss-of-function mutations in CHSY1 and VCAN both disrupt proteoglycan biosynthesis, which in turn leads to aberrant extracellular matrix organization, ultimately manifesting as skeletal dysplasia in Temtamy preaxial brachydactyly syndrome and retinal abnormalities in Wagner disease.

**How to falsify it:** Discovery of pathogenic variants in CHSY1 or VCAN with a minor allele frequency > 0.1% in gnomAD. _(variant: CHSY1 or VCAN pathogenic variants)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of CHSY1 and VCAN in extracellular matrix integrity could lead to therapeutic strategies targeting ECM repair or modulation for both skeletal and ocular manifestations.

#### 7. congenital stromal corneal dystrophy  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.424)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-3595177, Reactome:R-HSA-2022870)

**Proposed mechanism:** CHSY1 (HGNC:2364) —DISRUPTS→ Extracellular matrix proteoglycan synthesis and organization (GO:0000226); DCN (HGNC:2753) —DISRUPTS→ Extracellular matrix proteoglycan synthesis and organization (GO:0000226); Extracellular matrix proteoglycan synthesis and organization (GO:0000226) —LEADS_TO→ Preaxial brachydactyly (HP:0001748); Extracellular matrix proteoglycan synthesis and organization (GO:0000226) —LEADS_TO→ Corneal opacity (HP:0000539). Mutations in CHSY1 and DCN disrupt the synthesis and organization of extracellular matrix proteoglycans, leading to the distinct but related phenotypes of preaxial brachydactyly and corneal opacity.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of pathogenic variants in CHSY1 or DCN with significantly different functional consequences (e.g., gain-of-function vs. loss-of-function) for each disease, or demonstration that mutations in CHSY1 and DCN affect entirely distinct cellular pathways that do not converge. _(variant: Presence of common, likely benign variants in CHSY1 or DCN in relevant populations within gnomAD that are associated with either phenotype.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of CHSY1 and DCN in extracellular matrix organization could reveal common therapeutic targets for skeletal dysplasias and corneal dystrophies. Modulating proteoglycan synthesis or degradation could offer a unified approach to treating these conditions.
